case_title: Rohtash Kumar v. State of Haryana
weapon: Rope found near the body; death by smothering and throttling
evidence_type: Circumstantial (last seen together, call records, recovery of phone, guest house conduct, FSL hair comparison); medical (post-mortem); recovery memos; oral testimony
confession: No formal confession. Telephone calls from the victim's phone to relatives in which the accused said he had killed her were relied on as evidence. Diary and letter writings were also relied on as admissions of motive.
aggravating_circumstances: Killing of the spouse by smothering and throttling; accused fled, used a fictitious identity, attempted suicide, and made calls to relatives claiming the killing
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 and s.404; life imprisonment and Rs 5,000 fine under s.302 (one year default); two years RI and Rs 500 fine under s.404; sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed (Criminal Appeal No. 862-DB of 2006, judgment dated 5.2.2009); conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim had married, and the marriage was not approved by the victim's family and was strained. The couple had started divorce proceedings by mutual consent, with the second hearing listed for the following day. On the day before that hearing, the accused visited the hostel where the victim lived and worked. The two spoke for about an hour in the verandah, after which the accused left alone. Later, the victim was found dead among plants in the hostel grounds. The victim's father, who came to the hostel, was told by hostel staff that the accused had visited. A complaint was lodged, and police recovered the body and nearby objects, including a rope. The post-mortem examination found death by asphyxia caused by smothering and throttling, with neck abrasions and fractures of the neck and chest. Calls were later made from the victim's mobile phone to her mother and other relatives, in which the caller said he had killed her and would commit suicide. The accused was traced to a guest house, where he had registered under a fictitious name and address. He tried to end his life there and ran away, leaving a diary, a letter and a wrist watch, which contained writings about his grievances with the victim's family. The victim's mobile phone was later recovered from a shop in another state, following the accused's disclosure, and call records showed it was used after the death. Hair found at the scene was reported as similar to the accused's sample. The accused declined a test identification parade.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by asphyxia from smothering and throttling; neck abrasions, contusions, fracture of thyroid cartilage and tracheal rings, and bilateral clavicle and rib fractures
financial_property_loss: Victim's mobile phone taken by the accused and later recovered; no monetary loss stated
premeditation_planning: Not expressly found; the court noted the accused met the victim just before the divorce date but recorded no finding of planning
motive: Accepted by the court: the accused's feelings of grievance against the victim and her family, drawn from the undelivered letter and the diary suicide note, and marital discord leading to the proposed divorce
key_evidence_accepted: Last-seen evidence of the hostel caretaker; post-mortem findings; call records and calls to relatives; recovery of the victim's phone after disclosure; diary, letter and wrist watch; guest house stay under fake name; FSL hair report; refusal of test identification parade
witness_credibility: Caretaker (PW.8) found independent and reliable, with no reason to doubt her statement. Hostile witness (PW.2) accepted in part where his evidence was consistent with prosecution case. Discrepancies held not material.
post_offence_conduct: Absconded for several days; stayed at a guest house under a fictitious name and address; attempted suicide and fled when chased; made calls to relatives about the killing; phone recovered after disclosure; refused test identification parade
trial_duration: offence: 2.9.2004; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 5.2.2009; Supreme Court: 29.5.2013
legal_representation: Appellant: Dr. Sushil Balwada, Pankaj Bhagat. State: Ramesh Kumar, Manish K. Bishnoi
investigation_status: FIR registered on complaint; investigation, post-mortem and FSL report completed; chargesheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: appeal dismissed on 5.2.2009. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Accused was last seen with the victim and left alone just before her death; he fled, used a fake name at a guest house, attempted suicide and left incriminating writings; conduct shows guilt; concurrent findings should not be disturbed
defence_argument: No eye-witness and circumstantial chain incomplete; divorce was to be finalised the next day so no motive; key guard, cook and guest house witnesses not examined; hostile witness evidence unusable; last-seen theory inapplicable; phone recovery far away; material inconsistencies
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain consistent only with guilt; last seen together shifts burden to accused to explain death; motive relevant; s.313 explanation and false explanation as missing link; evidence weighed not counted; hostile and police witness evidence assessed with caution; minor discrepancies ignored
precedent_relied_upon: R. Shaji v. State of Kerala, AIR 2013 SC 651; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1984 SC 1622; Paramjeet Singh v. State of Uttarakhand, AIR 2011 SC 200; State of Maharashtra v. Suresh, (2000) 1 SCC 471; Nika Ram v. State of Himachal Pradesh, AIR 1972 SC 2077; Ganeshlal v. State of Maharashtra, (1992) 3 SCC 106; Trimukh Maroti Kirkan v. State of Maharashtra, (2006) 10 SCC 681; Pradeep Narayan Madgaonkar v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1995 SC 1930
judicial_aggravating_factors: Court described the killing as a heinous crime arising from marital discord; no other aggravating factors weighed separately
